items.title: UDF setback as LDF wrests seven wards in Keralam local body bypolls
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) suffered a setback in Keralam’s local body bye-elections, with the Left Democratic Front (LDF) wresting seven wards from it. Two of the wards had been vacated by sitting UDF MLAs. The UDF won 19 of the 38 wards, while the opposition LDF won 18. Twenty20, an ally of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), won the remaining seat. Before the bye-elections, the UDF held 22 of the wards, the LDF 15, and the NDA one. Bye-elections were held across 38 local body wards in 12 districts of Keralam, excluding Kollam and Alappuzha. The results mark the first major electoral test for the VD Satheesan-led UDF government. The UDF retained key wards including the Ayyappankkavu division in the Kochi Corporation and Kuttichira in the Kozhikode Corporation. However, its margin in Kuttichira was lower than in the previous election. The LDF’s gains included seven wards wrested from the UDF across districts including Kannur, Kottayam, Palakkad, and Thiruvananthapuram. The seats captured by the LDF include the the Thrikkodithanam Division of the Kottayam District

Govind Mohan ]. In an order passed on Tuesday, a Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and AS Chandurkar noted that the matter had been deleted from the afternoon roster during the lunch recess, despite standing judicial orders mandating its listing at 2:00 PM. "The Court has been informed at 2 pm that the case has been struck off from the cause list during the lunch break. items.title: ‘Savukku’ Shankar gets 3-year jail term in defamation case filed by former newsreader
items.summary: YouTuber ‘Savukku’ Shankar has been convicted in a defamation case filed by former Sun TV news reader and advocate Mahalakshmi. A Chennai court on Tuesday, September 29, sentenced Shankar to three years in prison and imposed a fine of Rs 20,000. Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sivashakthi found Shankar guilty under Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with words or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman, and Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. The court also granted Shankar 30 days to appeal against the verdict. Mahalakshmi had first lodged a complaint against Shankar in 2013, alleging that he had published defamatory remarks about her on his website, ‘Savukku’. She subsequently approached the Egmore court, accusing Shankar and his associates of threatening her, defaming her and fabricating documents. During the proceedings, Mahalakshmi’s lawyer argued that Shankar had deliberately published defamatory allegations against her and issued threats, and sought legal action against him.
